VIDEO PROMPTING · 12 MIN

AI Video Prompting: Camera, Continuity and Sound.

Turn an idea into a sequence that a video model can execute consistently.

Published September 3, 2026Editorial team · PromptStudio AI

Video prompting adds time, motion and sound to visual direction. A good prompt does not merely describe a beautiful frame; it describes what changes and what remains consistent across the shot.

IN THIS GUIDE1. Define one shot before defining a film2. Use camera movement with purpose3. Protect continuity and physics4. Direct sound as a separate layer

Define one shot before defining a film

Begin with a single action, camera move and duration. “The camera slowly tracks beside the vehicle as it enters morning fog” is easier to execute than a paragraph containing five locations and six cuts.

For a multi-shot sequence, label each shot and keep transitions explicit. Reintroduce immutable subject details when consistency is critical.

Use camera movement with purpose

A dolly-in increases attention. A lateral tracking move reveals shape and motion. A locked camera emphasizes performance within the frame. Choose one dominant movement and describe speed and stability.

Avoid stacking crane, orbit, zoom and handheld movement unless the sequence truly requires it. Conflicting camera verbs often produce unstable geometry.

Protect continuity and physics

State what must remain consistent: face, wardrobe, vehicle geometry, product packaging, weather and time of day. Mention realistic weight, cloth behavior, reflections and contact with surfaces.

Use a first-frame or reference image when the model supports it. For image-to-video, specify which objects may move and which should remain fixed.

Direct sound as a separate layer

List ambience, synchronized effects, dialogue and music separately. If speech matters, keep the line short and define speaker, tone and environment.

Review visual and audio continuity independently. Native audio can sound convincing while containing incorrect words or effects, so final editing remains essential.

KEY TAKEAWAYS
  • Keep each shot executable.
  • Choose one dominant camera move.
  • State continuity constraints.
  • Describe physical behavior.
  • Direct and review audio separately.
